title: Invocation schema validator and suggested remediations
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Design and implement a compact JSON invocation schema validator and an error/ remediation catalog for tool/function calls. Goal: provide deterministic validation behavior across Hosted/Dedicated/Private runtimes, clear machine-readable error codes, and actionable human remediation hints so SDKs + Console can surface high quality guidance to integrators without leaking low-level runtime internals.
goals: Define a constrained JSON-schema subset (Shape DSL) that covers common tool parameter needs without the complexity of full JSON Schema drafts.
Implement three validation modes (strict reject, best-effort coercion, and soft-warn) selectable by route and by customer tier.
Produce an error catalog with stable error codes (TC_XXX) and structured remediation hints for SDKs/console.
Emit telemetry for validation outcomes to enable SLOs and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
Provide a migration path for existing tool manifests and backward-compatible fallbacks for older SDKs.
design_decisions: Use a lightweight Shape DSL derived from core JSON Schema types: object, array, string, number, boolean, enum. Omit advanced features (patternProperties, $ref, allOf/oneOf) to keep validators deterministic and fast.
Validators run in two places: pre-runtime (API gateway / compiler) and runtime (serving node) to avoid incorrect acceptance due to compiler-only checks.
Introduce explicit 'coerce' annotation for fields that may accept strings but should be coerced to numbers/booleans. Coercion is opt-in to avoid silent data corruption.
Error codes will be 7-char prefixed tokens starting with TC_ (Tool Contract) and a 4-digit number (example: TC_1001). Codes are stable and referenced in docs and SDKs.
Human remediation hints are short sentences (<=140 chars) and include an example fix when practical. Hints are surfaced in Console and SDK error wrappers.
Default validation mode for new routes is 'coerce-typed' for smoother onboarding; enterprise customers can opt-in to 'reject-strict'.
validation_modes: reject-strict: Validation fails on any type/shape mismatch. Returns TC_1xxx errors. Intended for strict contracts and regulated workloads.
coerce-typed: Best-effort coercion for annotated fields (int<->string, bool strings). On failure, returns TC_2xxx with remediation hint and optionally a warning.
soft-warn: Always accept the payload; emit TC_3xxx telemetry and warnings but proceed. Useful for experiments and phased rollouts.
error_catalog: TC_1001: missing_required_field - A required field is absent.
TC_1002: type_mismatch - Field value is wrong type and coercion not enabled.
TC_1003: enum_violation - Value not allowed in declared enum.
TC_2001: coercion_failed - Coercion attempted but unsuccessful (example: 'abc' -> number).
TC_3001: extra_field_ignored - Payload contains fields not declared in schema (warning mode).
TC_4001: array_length_out_of_bounds - Array length outside min/max constraints.
remediation_hints: TC_1001 -> Add the missing field and ensure it matches the declared type. Example: {"timeout": 30 }.
TC_1002 -> Convert the value to the expected type or mark the schema field with "coerce": true if safe.
TC_1003 -> Choose one of the allowed enum values; check documentation for valid options.
TC_2001 -> Provide a correctly typed value or remove the field if optional.
TC_3001 -> Remove unsupported fields or update the schema to accept additional keys if intended.
TC_4001 -> Ensure array length is within the declared min/max or use batching to split requests.
acceptance_criteria: Shape DSL spec document merged in docs/runtime/tooling with examples and edge cases.
Reference validator library implemented in Go (runtime) and TypeScript (SDK) with feature parity.
Error catalog published and linked from Console error details with remediation hints visible in failure UI.
Telemetry events emitted for each validation outcome and visible in internal dashboards within 24 hours of rollout.
Backward-compatibility tests covering 3 months of historical tool manifests with no more than 1% new rejection rate during canary.

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary, 2% traffic): Deploy validators in coerce-typed mode for new routes only. Monitor validation.result and TC_2xxx rates.
Phase 2 (Ramp, 25%): Enable pre-runtime validation in gateway for all routes with opt-out via route flag. Begin SDK warnings for TC_3xxx.
Phase 3 (Default, 100%): Set default to coerce-typed for new customers, allow enterprise to choose reject-strict. Start hard-reject for legacy deprecated routes after 90 days.
Rollback: Toggle route flags to bypass pre-runtime validation or switch to soft-warn if regressions spike above 5% error budget.
telemetry: validation.code (string): stable TC_xxxx code for the specific predicate that fired
route (string): API route or model route name
sdk_version (string): SDK that submitted the payload
latency_ms (number as string): time spent validating (for perf monitoring)
sdk_behavior: SDKs will map TC_XXXX to user-friendly exceptions with remediation_hint attached.
TypeScript SDK will perform client-side pre-validation using same Shape DSL; errors surfaced synchronously where possible.
Python SDK will expose a ValidationMode enum and helpers to convert/normalize payloads using coercion annotations.
SDKs log compact telemetry to aid debugging in customer environments (opt-in for private deployments).
migration_notes: Run manifest-migrate tool that attempts safe coercions and emits a preview diff for developers to review.
Mark routes deprecated with deprecation warning events for 90 days before enforcing stricter validation.
Provide a nightly report of rejected manifests to the owning teams to remediate contract drift.
